# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS (for answering questions without the original)

## Format
Two Project Gutenberg texts by Grace May North, both illustrated by Florence Liley Young, published by Lothrop, Lee & Shepard (Boston). Book 1: *Adele Doring at Boarding-School* (1921, gutenberg 62360, 30 chapters). Book 2: *Adele Doring of the Sunnyside Club* (1919, gutenberg 62151, 33 chapters). Book 1 is a sequel-type continuation of Book 2's characters, though Book 2 is set first (spring to autumn in Sunnyside). Book 1's text is set in the fall after Book 2 ends with the Sunny Seven's summer camp plans. Book 1 ends with "Adele Doring out camping!" Book 2 ends with a "next chapter" pointer to *Adele Doring on a Ranch*.

---

## BOOK 1: ADELE DORING AT BOARDING-SCHOOL

**Dedication:** to girls in the "Sunnyside Club of California" and to the author's readers.

**Chapters:** I A New Sunnysider; II The Ogre; III Two Surprises; IV New Faces and New Places; V A Letter from Carol; VI Betty's Uncle George; VII The Departure for Boarding-School; VIII Apple-Blossom Alley; IX Gladys Merle's Clique; X The Downfall of Gladys Merle; XI True Nobility; XII A Wish Fulfilled; XIII The New Teacher; XIV Orphan Alise; XV The Grandfather of Alise; XVI Taming Katrina; XVII An Unexpected Spread; XVIII A Thanksgiving Dinner Party; XIX Just Skipping Along; XX The Old-Fashioned Pupil; XXI The Prairie Home; XXII Lady Stuckup; XXIII A Dream that Came True; XXIV The C. E. P.; XXV A String of Pearls; XXVI Romancing; XXVII Old Friends Arrive; XXVIII The Closing Party; XXIX A Bud of a Romance; XXX Farewell, Linden Hall.

### Ch 1 (Sunnyside, Sept.)
- **Adele Doring**, 14, eighth grade, rose-colored tam and sweater-coat, nut-brown curls. Mother ("Mumsie", "Adorable Mother"), father ("Giant Daddy"), brother Jack (goes to Dorchester High next year). Last summer she visited Arizona with Eva and Amanda at Uncle Dick's ranch.
- **Rosamond "Rosie" Wright**: short yellow curls, dislikes study.
- **Carol Lorens**, 15, new girl from the Middle West (Chicago suburb). Father a lawyer who lost fortune; family moved to father's boyhood farmhouse on Lake Road, apple orchard. Mother; brother **Peter** (gave up college); twins **David** and **Dorothy** (7). Principal **Mr. Dickerson** says Carol must attend Dorchester High.
- **Betty Burd**: irrepressible, "Bettykins". Gertrude Willis, Doris Drexel named; the "Sunny Seven"/"Sunny Six" club group.

### Ch 2 (The Ogre)
- Carol's mother: "The right way always opens." Carol wants boarding-school for music and drawing; Peter gave up college for money reasons.
- Errand: legal papers to **Mr. Dartmoor**, wealthy old client; "ogre" per Peter. Estate with stone lions at steps, archway. Twins wait at fountain. Mr. Dartmoor has grey shaggy eyebrows, twinkling blue eyes, cane.
- Granddaughter **Evelyn Dartmoor**, 15, portrait with shaggy collie; at boarding-school near **Buffalo**; mother recently died; parents dead.
- Dorothy: "Why don't you cry?"; Carol's "silver lining" idea.
- Carol vows never to leave mother.

### Ch 3 (Two Surprises)
- Evelyn's letter to Granddad: lonely; roommate issue; **Madame Deriby** (school head) insists on roommate.
- Mr. Dartmoor visits Lorens home; offers Carol place at **Linden Hall Seminary** as Evelyn's roommate/companion. Dorothy offers to help mother.
- Sunny Seven meeting: Carol at elm-tree; Doris Drexel had met Evelyn.

### Ch 4 (New Faces and New Places)
- Carol departs by train, 9 a.m.; father's advice: "What would my mother do?"
- Arrives at **Linden** station (two hours to Buffalo, then local train). Evelyn: tall, slender, in black. Mr. Dartmoor and Carol's grandfather were "pals."
- Linden Hall: elm-lined drive, colonial mansion, lake view.

### Ch 5 (A Letter from Carol)
- Carol's letter read aloud at the elm-tree. Describes Madame Deriby ("tall, stately, silvery hair"). Room yellow; 40 pupils.
- Mr. Dickerson: teacher Miss Donovan has left (mother ill); eighth grade must go to Dorchester. Girls then decide to go to Linden Hall. Meeting at log cabin "Secret Sanctum" (the cabin is introduced in Book 2).
- Bertha Angel's father approves college prep; Peggy Pierce, Doris Drexel can go. Betty cannot (Uncle George costs). Gertrude stays home (father minister; she tutors Betty).

### Ch 6 (Betty's Uncle George)
- Betty's pony ride; **Uncle George** (Wainwright; editor, young, "Puss", "Betty Bobbets"). Father was George's older brother; George pays. Betty hugs him.
- Madame Deriby writes: room for five; school bus at Buffalo station Saturday at 4 p.m.

### Ch 7 (The Departure)
- Sunnyside station; **Uncle Danny** station master, deaf. Jensen candy boxes (Dick Jensen; "Jolly Pirates"). Jack and Bob Angel tease. Six girls leave.

### Ch 8 (Apple-Blossom Alley)
- Letter from Adele to Carol; girls arrive Saturday 4:30. Madame Deriby, "the matron."
- Room corridor named Apple-Blossom Alley (walls with apple blossoms, suggested by Rosamond). Evelyn and Carol move into the south wing with friends.
- Evelyn: **Gladys Merle Jones**, daughter of Chicago "Beef King," leads snobbish clique; Janet Nagel is in her clique. Miss Sharpleigh teacher. Bertha: "father a grocer"; Peggy: "dad's dry-goods store".

### Ch 9 (Gladys Merle's Clique)
- Clique: Anita Ryan (echoes Gladys), Janet Nagel, Jenny Clark. Anita writes to her aunt in Sunnyside asking about the newcomers (Gladys says Madame Deriby does not read all letters).
- Night: Patrick O'Neil and **Billie** (Bill) gardener/stable boy; Gladys and Anita flee to mail the letter at the gate; Bill sees them: "Huh! Nothin' but girls."

### Ch 10 (The Downfall of Gladys Merle)
- Aunt's reply intercepted: via Miss Sharpleigh reading letters; "Aunt Laura" letter says Carol is a poor lawyer's daughter sent as paid companion for Dartmoor's granddaughter.
- Janet defends Carol; Gladys boasts her father is handsome/stately. Janet deserts clique. Adele snubs Gladys.

### Ch 11 (True Nobility)
- Gladys's father, Mr. Jones (short, stout, red-faced, uneducated rancher), visits Linden Hall; Gladys hides and refuses to come out. Gladys plans to leave.
- Carol visits; tells of great-grandfather who refused royal title from the King of England; "The Making of Royalty." Gladys apologizes; reunites with Carol. Gladys visits father in Buffalo.

### Ch 12 (A Wish Fulfilled)
- Girls interviewed by Madame Deriby. Bertha: Latin and French. Betty: "adore her."
- Kindergarten teacher **Miss Berry** leaves (brother ill); Madame Deriby wants older girl to teach little ones for tuition. Adele recommends Gertrude; letter sent.

### Ch 13 (The New Teacher)
- Gertrude arrives Saturday; phone call from **Mr. Willis**. Train stuck on siding; Patrick drives girls to fetch Gertrude by bus. Gertrude takes Miss Berry's class (ages 5–7).

### Ch 14 (Orphan Alise)
- Little **Alise**, six, golden hair, brown eyes, orphan; mother married against stern father; grandfather refused to see child. Gertrude "big sister" to Alise.
- Riding class with **Mr. Haley** (riding-master). **Elmhurst** estate; marble statue of a young girl; pedestal name "Alise [...] El[lsworth]".

### Ch 15 (The Grandfather of Alise)
- Gertrude sees trunk labeled "A. R. Ellsworth." Gertrude and Adele ride to Elmhurst (Mrs. Diggitt, lodge). Portrait of stern old man. Lad **Arthur Ellsworth**, ~18; **Aunt Louise** (pale, beautiful), sister of Alise's mother. Alise Alderly named. Aunt Louise recognizes Alise.

### Ch 16 (Taming Katrina)
- **Katrina Mason**: spoiled, fretful; Carol visits her; play; Carol gives her summer-girl part; Katrina shares Thanksgiving goodies; "loving kindness."

### Ch 17 (An Unexpected Spread)
- Girls visit Katrina ("Iceland"). Feast on floor; Katrina apologizes; Gertrude invited. Rehearsals at four-thirty.

### Ch 18 (A Thanksgiving Dinner Party)
- Ellsworth invitation; dinner Thanksgiving. Bob and Jack, Donald Burnley, Dick Jensen disguised as "Russians" (Mr. Mellowisky; Rose recognizes Bob). Chrysanthemums from Arthur. Arthur seems to like Gertrude.

### Ch 19 (Just Skipping Along)
- Sleigh-ride party at Elmhurst (Alise's birthday). Carol plays Irish maid Norah in the play; presented pink carnations.
- Adele enters French essay medal contest; Marie Le Clerc wins.
- Gladys Merle's birthday theater party in Buffalo.
- March: new pupil.

### Ch 20 (The Old-Fashioned Pupil)
- **Matilda Perkins** (later "Starr"), 15, from Dakota prairie; plaid shawl, beaver cap, mittens; sent by **Bishop Wesley**. Assigned to room with **Geraldine Barrington** ("Lady Stuckup"), English. Gertrude "take her under my wing."

### Ch 21 (The Prairie Home)
- Matilda's story: brothers **Cedric** (oldest) and **Basil** (younger); dog **Shep**; mother's Bible and picture; blizzard; Bishop rescued and grateful. Bishop's sister married Margaret Inslay (Matilda's mother). Adele gives Matilda uniform; names her "Starr."

### Ch 22 (Lady Stuckup)
- Geraldine's rant; asks to move; Matilda offered cupola room. Peggy's invented haunted-cupola story (Nina Best). Geraldine reads Matilda's diary. Matilda finds **Geraldine** injured near wood (arbutus); farmer O'Rourke helps.

### Ch 23 (A Dream that Came True)
- Matilda nurses Geraldine. Geraldine apologizes; Mr. Barrington (Geraldine's father) returns; Matilda is his sister's (Inslay) daughter. Barringtons of Ivondale; Barrington Manor.

### Ch 24 (The C. E. P.)
- "C. E. P." = closing-exercise party; Gertrude's 16th birthday surprise planned. Adele's secret.

### Ch 25 (A String of Pearls)
- Gertrude's Uncle Pierson's $20; Gertrude bought mother a dress; pearls fund; Evelyn treasurer. Betty's pink muslin dress altered by Adele.

### Ch 26 (Romancing)
- Eva Dearman coming from Arizona. Jack's letter: Uncle Jack's island in St. Lawrence River for camping in August. Madge Petersen to chaperone.

### Ch 27 (Old Friends Arrive)
- Madge and **Everett Petersen**, Eva arrive. Arthur meets Everett.

### Ch 28 (The Closing Party)
- Rosamond's pink rose; Starr's silver star; party in recreation hall; Hawaiian musicians.

### Ch 29 (A Bud of a Romance)
- Surprise birthday song; string of "friendship pearls" from Betty. Orchard lanterns. Arthur proposes-ish to Gertrude; she declines accepting help, "if you do care when we are older."

### Ch 30 (Farewell, Linden Hall)
- Goodbye; song "Farewell, Dear Linden Hall." Last line: "Adele Doring out camping!"

---

## BOOK 2: ADELE DORING OF THE SUNNYSIDE CLUB

**Dedication:** to Margaret Edna Rock and happy-hearted girls 10–15.

**Chapters:** I The Sunnyside Club; II The Secret Sanctum; III A Jolly Scrubbing-Party; IV Adele's Secret; V Pleasant Plans; VI A Surprise Party; VII A Birthday Feast; VIII More Surprises; IX The Mother Goose Play-House; X Preparing for Examinations; XI Vacation Days; XII The Fudge Party; XIII The Two Dryads; XIV Pine Island; XV An Exciting Adventure; XVI More Mystery; XVII The Little Bear; XVIII A Fish Supper; XIX A Trip to the City; XX Amanda Brown; XXI The Ball Game; XXII The King's Highway; XXIII School-Days Again; XXIV The House by the Wood; XXV A Visit to the Poorhouse; XXVI A Mystery Solved; XXVII A Really, Truly Home; XXVIII The New Pupil; XXIX Eva Begins a New Life; XXX Eva Humiliated; XXXI Something Unexpected; XXXII A Happy Meeting; XXXIII Farewell to the Orphanage.

### Ch 1 (The Sunnyside Club) – April
- Seven girls: Adele Doring (president, "Heart's Desire" to Giant Father), Rosamond Wright (romantic, tatting), Bertha Angel (treasurer; practical; father grocer; brother Bob), Gertrude Willis (secretary; minister's daughter), Betty Burd (youngest, "Bettykins", "Little One"; widowed mother; Uncle George), Peggy Pierce (father owns Bee Hive dept store), Doris Drexel (father bank president; hates math).
- Pussy-willows; stone wall. Pledge: "We promise to look on the Sunnyside / And be kind and cheerful each day; / To help the needy or lonely or sad, / Whom we happen to meet on our way."
- Club motto (later): "The only creed of which we have need is the art of being kind."

### Ch 2 (The Secret Sanctum)
- Log cabin in Buttercup Meadows, near maple wood and laughing brook, Lookout Hill; built for sheep-herders by Adele's grandfather. Adele's father gives it. Key under log. Rustic furniture.

### Ch 3 (A Jolly Scrubbing-Party)
- Cook **Kate** (Irish, Doring cook); Jack eats chocolate cupcakes. Adele's black pony **Firefly**, red cart. Terrence, handyman. Robin's song.
- Furnishing list: mosquito netting; mattress; pine pillow (Doris); blue bowl (Rosamond); china-closet from orange boxes; bank.

### Ch 4 (Adele's Secret)
- Adele visits **Granny Dorset** (cottage in Cherry Lane, bed-ridden) with violets. Adele's birthday next week (13). Orphanage girl Eva Dearman's birthday surprise planned.

### Ch 5 (Pleasant Plans)
- **Eva Dearman**: father broker lost money; mother died; deed to desert property in Arizona; to be 13. **Amanda Brown**: surly, unpopular.
- Bank hidden under shed loose board — gone; Peggy had taken it to her father's safe. Mr. Pierce sells necklaces with lockets at cost ($6.33 total fund).

### Ch 6 (A Surprise Party)
- Eva's birthday in orphanage. Amanda locked in linen-closet crying (Jenny Dixon said unkind things); Eva insists.
- Hayrack with daisies, horses **Jerry and Jingo**, driver Bob Angel. Adele: "Lovely Queen o' May!" Party: lettuce sandwiches, chicken salad, birthday cake with 13 pink candy roses. Jack and Bob as black waiters ("Rastus"). Lockets for the 12 orphans.

### Ch 7 (A Birthday Feast) — see Ch 6 above (chapter 7 covers the feast).

### Ch 8 (More Surprises)
- Adele home alone; Jack, Kate away; Jolly Pirates surprise party in library. Gifts: set "Stories That Girls Like Best" (from Sunny Six); fern from Jolly Pirates; Heart's Desire writing-desk from Giant Father; Mother's painting of log cabin. Birthday cake with salt in it from Kate; fortunes: Dick straw, Doris thimble, Jack silver dime, Rosamond wedding ring ("first bride").

### Ch 9 (The Mother Goose Play-House)
- Mrs. Friend (matron). Gertrude and Adele visit orphans' nursery (twenty children, ages 5–8). Gardener's cottage to be play-house. Betty's Mother Goose box from her late father (architect) fitted with cloth pictures. Jack and Bob deliver it. Fudge party promised.

### Ch 10 (Preparing for Examinations)
- Betty's Uncle George (**George Wainwright**, editor) sells a story for $100; bribes Betty with pony if she passes perfect in spelling/grammar. Pony later named **Star**. Mr. Dickerson's oral test cancelled. Betty passes grammar/spelling; Miss Donovan teacher.

### Ch 11 (Vacation Days)
- Adele asks mother for Eva's visit; Mrs. Friend lends Eva. Adele's room: wild-rose wallpaper; blue bowl with dragon from Uncle Dixon (Japan). Jack: "Pirate the Terrible."

### Ch 12 (The Fudge Party)
- Dorings' Giant Father; Kate. Jolly Pirates (seven boys) with black cloth, "Fifteen men on a dead man's chest." Rosie sees "ghost" at cross-roads (whitewashed tree trunk). Boys: Bob Angel, Dick Jensen, Lawrence Collins, Donald Burnley (also "Donald"), Jack.

### Ch 13 (The Two Dryads)
- Adele and Eva climb Lookout Hill at dawn. **Madge Peterson** (painter, 18) and brother **Everett**; sailboat tips at Pine Island; Eva "Dryad Fern," Adele "Dryad Oakleaf." Little Bear Lake Inn; Ching Ling cook.

### Ch 14 (Pine Island)
- Picnic on Pine Island: fried chicken, lettuce sandwiches, olives, chocolate cake.

### Ch 15 (An Exciting Adventure)
- Everett and Adele see a "wild man" in bear skin digging treasure (Ben Gunn) — actually the Jolly Pirates playing Treasure Island with boys (Pirate the Terrible = Jack). Flag with skull and crossbones.

### Ch 16 (More Mystery)
- Eva and Madge; Madge offers art lessons at Art Institute. Fisherman's boat taken; fisherman (Jock Henderson) tells story of **Little Bear**.

### Ch 17 (The Little Bear)
- Jock Henderson raised **Eric Brownley** (Kid), a bear cub Little Bear; Eric's uncle in city; Eric to city school. Little Bear dies from poison.

### Ch 18 (A Fish Supper)
- Eric Brownley, Everett's school friend ("Petey"). Trout fried. Uncle George Wainwright gives car ride; Madge illustrates Miss Kimberly's children's verse.

### Ch 19 (A Trip to the City)
- Madge takes Eva to Art Institute; Pigmy (her car). Amanda's birthday; Eva brings her along.

### Ch 20 (Amanda Brown)
- Amanda's mother a singer; old singing-master (sings with Amanda).

### Ch 21 (The Ball Game)
- North High vs South High; Eric pitches for North High; Dorset (sub) pitched first. Eric arrives on horse from Bear Lake.

### Ch 22 (The King's Highway)
- Madge's letter ("Dear Dryad Oakleaf"); Gertrude to Art Institute. Roberty-Bob (hunchbacked boy, wheel chair, Muffin the kitten, goldfish), "God is the King... His Highway is wherever you are." Gertrude's composition on "The King's Highway" (Alicia story).

### Ch 23 (School-Days Again)
- Seventh grade; Miss Donovan returns as teacher. Club plans Granny Dorset's 70th birthday party; wants purple silk dress with lace. Peggy & Rosie committee.

### Ch 24 (The House by the Wood)
- Gertrude and Adele visit Granny Dorset (Grandpa 'Lijah Dally, Mr. Quigley, Mrs. Quigley). Miss Sally Grackle (lives alone in cottage by woods; sister Miranda eloped to Arizona). Girls bring broth. Miss Grackle agrees to come.

### Ch 25 (A Visit to the Poorhouse)
- Mrs. Quigley (Betsy), Pa Quigley (Dan). Grandpa Dally's miser story (long lank man, gold, cabin). Miss Grackle decides to let Quigleys live in cottage.

### Ch 26 (A Mystery Solved)
- Chipmunk knocks gold piece from behind fireplace; bag of gold ($1,000) and note. Deposited at Mr. Drexel's bank (First National). Cottage prepared.

### Ch 27 (A Really, Truly Home)
- Surprise party; Bob Angel and Gertrude fetch Quigleys. Granny Dorset gets purple silk dress. Grandpa Dally's wolf story. Quigleys given cottage.

### Ch 28 (The New Pupil)
- **Susetta Green** (father **Cyrus Green**, mother **Melissa**; former tavern keeper from the West; Restwell estate). Susie snubs girls; pink invitations to select party refused by five girls.
- Mrs. Green visits orphanage; chooses **Eva** as companion/maid for Susetta.

### Ch 29 (Eva Begins a New Life)
- Board of directors: Eva must go. Eva's Uncle Dick Dearman: letter to Dry Creek, Arizona.

### Ch 30 (Eva Humiliated)
- Eva as servant: black dress, cap and apron. Susetta; Mrs. Green forbids Adele and Doris from visiting Eva. Mrs. Doring proposes adopting Eva.

### Ch 31 (Something Unexpected)
- Adele meets **Richard "Uncle Dick" Dearman** (cattle king, Silver Creek, Bar-X Ranch) outside orphanage; goes to Restwell. Mr. Green: "Well, Dick Dearman!" Mrs. Green pretends kindness.

### Ch 32 (A Happy Meeting)
- Eva reunited with Uncle Dick; Mrs. Green hides; Eva's satchel. Eva invited to stay at Dorings; Adele invited to visit ranch next summer.

### Ch 33 (Farewell to the Orphanage)
- Eva and Amanda both go west with Uncle Dick. Mrs. Friend consents. Trains to Douglas/Silver Creek. Adele: "living in a story-book... next chapter." Note: "Adele Doring on a Ranch" continues.

---

## Key recurring names (both books)
Adele Doring; Mumsie; Giant Daddy/Giant Father; Jack Doring; Kate (cook); Firefly (pony); Eva Dearman; Amanda Brown; Mrs. Friend; Uncle Dick Dearman; Madge & Everett Petersen; Eric Brownley ("Petey" is Everett); Gertrude Willis; Bertha & Bob Angel; Rosamond Wright; Peggy Pierce; Doris Drexel; Betty Burd & Uncle George Wainwright; Granny Dorset; Miss Grackle; Mr. Drakely (postman); Miss Donovan (teacher); Mr. Dickerson (principal).
